es.summary: Linfoma de zona marginal extranodal (MALT) es un linfoma B de bajo grado asociado a estimulación crónica, frecuentemente por Helicobacter pylori.
key_points: Se origina en tejido linfoide asociado a mucosas (estómago, glándulas salivales, tiroides).
Infección por H. pylori y enfermedades autoinmunes son factores de riesgo principales.
El diagnóstico se confirma con biopsia y marcadores inmunohistoquímicos (CD20+, CD5‑, CD10‑).
El tratamiento de primera línea suele ser erradicación de H. pylori; radioterapia o rituximab en casos avanzados.

pathophysiology: Infección crónica (p. ej., H. pylori) produce estimulación antigénica persistente.
Activación y proliferación de linfocitos B marginales en la mucosa.
Acumulación de clones B neoplásicos forma tejido linfoide marginal (MALT).
Translocación t(11;18)(q21;q21) puede impedir la apoptosis y favorecer el crecimiento tumoral.
risk_factors: Enfermedades autoinmunes (síndrome de Sjögren, tiroiditis de Hashimoto).
Edad > 50 años y exposición a agentes inflamatorios crónicos.
signs_symptoms: Dolor o molestia epigástrica, dispepsia y pérdida de peso (cuando afecta estómago).
Masa indolora en glándulas salivales o tiroides.
Síntomas locales según el órgano involucrado (obstrucción, disfonía).
diagnostics: Endoscopia con biopsia y estudio histológico.
Prueba de aliento o serología para H. pylori.
TC o PET-CT para estadificación; LDH y hemograma de rutina.
treatment: Erradicación de H. pylori (amoxicilina + claritromicina + inhibidor de bomba de protones).
Radioterapia local (30‑36 Gy) para enfermedad localizada.
Quimioterapia con rituximab ± bendamustina en enfermedad avanzada.
complications: Transformación a linfoma de alto grado.
Obstrucción intestinal o biliar según localización.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor abdominal, tolerancia a la alimentación y signos de sangrado.
Monitorear temperatura, recuento de leucocitos y parámetros de función hepática/renal.
Administrar antibióticos para erradicación de H. pylori según prescripción.
Educar sobre signos de infección y sangrado gastrointestinal.
Apoyar nutrición adecuada; ofrecer dietas blandas si hay dispepsia.
patient_teaching: Completar el esquema completo de antibióticos aunque mejore el síntoma.
Evitar alimentos irritantes (picantes, alcohol, cafeína) durante el tratamiento.
Reportar sangrado rectal, vómito con sangre o fiebre persistente.
Programar controles endoscópicos y de laboratorio según indicación.

outcomes: Riesgo de infección reducido a < 5% durante el episodio de tratamiento

interventions.rationale: Detección temprana de fiebre permite intervención oportuna.

en.summary: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (MALT) is a low‑grade B‑cell lymphoma associated with chronic stimulation, frequently by Helicobacter pylori.
key_points: It originates in mucosa‑associated lymphoid tissue (stomach, salivary glands, thyroid).
H. pylori infection and autoimmune diseases are the main risk factors.
Diagnosis is confirmed with biopsy and immunohistochemical markers (CD20+, CD5‑, CD10‑).
First‑line treatment is usually eradication of H. pylori; radiotherapy or rituximab in advanced cases.

pathophysiology: Chronic infection (e.g., H. pylori) causes persistent antigenic stimulation.
Activation and proliferation of marginal zone B cells in the mucosa.
Accumulation of neoplastic B clones forms marginal zone lymphoid tissue (MALT).
Translocation t(11;18)(q21;q21) can inhibit apoptosis and promote tumor growth.
risk_factors: Age > 50 years and exposure to chronic inflammatory agents.
signs_symptoms: Epigastric pain or discomfort, dyspepsia, and weight loss (when stomach is involved).
Painless mass in salivary glands or thyroid.
Local symptoms depending on the involved organ (obstruction, dysphonia).
diagnostics: Endoscopy with biopsy and histologic examination.
Breath test or serology for H. pylori.
CT or PET‑CT for staging; routine LDH and CBC.
treatment: H. pylori eradication (amoxicillin + clarithromycin + proton‑pump inhibitor).
Local radiotherapy (30‑36 Gy) for localized disease.
Chemotherapy with rituximab ± bendamustine in advanced disease.
complications: Intestinal or biliary obstruction depending on location.
nursing_care: Assess abdominal pain, tolerance to eating, and signs of bleeding.
Monitor temperature, white blood cell count, and liver/renal function parameters.
Administer antibiotics for H. pylori eradication as prescribed.
Educate on signs of infection and gastrointestinal bleeding.
Support adequate nutrition; offer soft diets if dyspepsia is present.
patient_teaching: Complete the full antibiotic regimen even if symptoms improve.
Avoid irritating foods (spicy, alcohol, caffeine) during treatment.
Report rectal bleeding, vomiting with blood, or persistent fever.
Schedule endoscopic and laboratory follow‑ups as indicated.

outcomes: Infection risk reduced to <5% during the treatment episode

interventions.action: Assess vital signs every 4 h, focusing on temperature and respiratory rate.
interventions.rationale: Early detection of fever allows timely intervention.

interventions.action: Maintain hand hygiene and use gloves when handling invasive devices.
interventions.rationale: Prevents transmission of microorganisms to the immunocompromised patient.

interventions.action: Monitor white blood cell and neutrophil counts every 48 h during chemotherapy.
interventions.rationale: Identifies neutropenia that increases infection risk.

interventions.action: Educate patient and family on infection signs (fever, chills, purulent secretions).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early notification and treatment initiation.

interventions.rationale: Reduces exposure to environmental pathogens.

interventions.rationale: Provides a baseline to measure progress.

interventions.action: Coordinate with a dietitian to ensure adequate caloric and iron intake.
interventions.rationale: Corrects anemia and promotes energy.

interventions.action: Administer analgesia as prescribed before activities that cause pain.
interventions.rationale: Pain control allows greater participation in activity.

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing techniques to reduce dyspnea during exercise.
interventions.rationale: Optimizes oxygenation and decreases the sensation of shortness of breath.
